newsitem.title: UK: IEA says OPEC up, dismisses high Saudi output repo.
newsitem.headline: IEA says OPEC up, dismisses high Saudi output repo.

text.p: OPEC crude oil output in March rose 40,000 bpd from February to 27.09 million barrels per day (bpd), the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Tuesday.
The agency, in a monthly oil market report, estimated Saudi Arabian production at a lower 8.22 million bpd, including its share of the Neutral Zone, from 8.27 in February.
The IEA includes in its calculation of Saudi output almost 150,000 bpd of production in Saudi territory gifted to Bahrain.
The Paris-based agency dismissed some recent oil industry newsletter reports of a spike in Saudi output which it said "would not appear to be consistent with underlying Saudi oil policy."
"Recent Saudi pricing policy appears to be realistic but not aggressive, supporting the view of a relatively conservative Saudi approach to oil," it said.

It estimated Iraq had increased production by 100,000 bpd to 1.17 million bpd in March as exports surged to nearly a million bpd in early March to meet the $1 billion target for the first 90 days of the UN oil-for-food exchange.
